text: Anthropic has updated Claude Code Projects with proactive coordinator messages, read-only thread sharing, reminders, branching commands, and improved artifact navigation. The changes reduce the monitoring required when several cloud sessions work in parallel. Each project is a long-running conversation with a coordinator that assigns work to threads. Every thread runs as an independent Claude Code cloud session with its own repository copy and Git branch. The coordinator directs the project from thread reports, while overlapping code changes surface as standard Git merge conflicts when branches are combined. The coordinator now answers questions directly in project chat and posts status updates as threads progress. Previously, developers had to monitor the thread list to find sessions waiting for input. The updated behavior brings pending decisions, completed tasks, and blocked work into the main conversation. Individual threads can now be shared through read-only links with anyone signed in to Claude. A developer can open the thread menu, select Share , and send the generated URL without exposing the rest of the project. Threads that accessed a local computer remain unshareable. The restriction prevents shared transcripts from exposing local file contents, shell output, or other machine data gathered during the session. The two slash commands were already available in regular Claude Code sessions. Their addition to Projects brings the same branching workflow to coordinated, multi-thread work. The threads panel now places recently opened, updated, and pinned threads in a row at the top. Each thread can also display thumbnails for generated documents, diagrams, and other artifacts, with the previews controlled through view settings. The redesign simplifies project settings and local-folder access as well. Anthropic has released the changes on the web, desktop clients, and the latest mobile app. Anthropic introduced the public beta on September 17 for Pro and Max subscribers who joined the waitlist. Team and Enterprise plans remain unsupported. Eligible subscribers who lack access can still join the waitlist . Projects carry no separate fee, but every worker consumes the subscriber’s existing Claude Code allowance. Anthropic limits accounts to 200 new threads per day across all projects. A thread that reaches a usage limit pauses and resumes automatically when capacity becomes available. Project usage appears separately in the usage controls, and developers can choose the model and effort level for the coordinator and worker threads. New projects default to Opus for both roles, with low effort for the coordinator and high effort for workers. Several high-effort sessions running at once can exhaust plan limits faster than a single Claude Code session. Projects fit engineering work that can be divided into independent tasks and reconciled through branches and pull requests. Anthropic’s examples include: Tasks with strict dependencies still require developers to sequence pull requests and resolve conflicts. Projects also remain cloud-only and limited to Claude Code, while parallel workers draw from the same plan limits. Small changes that fit one branch and one context window generally consume fewer resources in a regular Claude Code session.
